Paths

GT_FOLDER, L1_FOLDER, and L2_FOLDER may each point to either:
  • A directory containing many files (the original behaviour), or
  • A single file to process in isolation.
Both forms are handled automatically by resolve_input_paths in the processing cells below -- no other configuration changes are required. Examples: 
# Directory of ground-truth label files (original behaviour)
GT_FOLDER = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/info_label_rev2"

# A single ground-truth label file
GT_FOLDER = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/info_label_rev2/00033.txt"

# Directory of os1-128 LiDAR PCDs (original behaviour)
L1_FOLDER = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/os1-128"

# A single os1-128 LiDAR PCD
L1_FOLDER = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/os1-128/os1-128_00033.pcd"

# Directory of os2-64 LiDAR PCDs (original behaviour)
L2_FOLDER = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/os2-64"

# A single os2-64 LiDAR PCD
L2_FOLDER = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/os2-64/os2-64_00033.pcd"

# Directory of radar zyx cubes (used by the Radar section)
RADAR_FOLDER = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/radar_zyx_cube"

# A single radar zyx cube (.mat)
RADAR_FOLDER = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/radar_zyx_cube/cube_00033.mat"

# Camera image folders (used by the Camera section)
CAM_FRONT_FOLDER  = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/cam_front"
CAM_LEFT_FOLDER   = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/cam_left"
CAM_RIGHT_FOLDER  = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/cam_right"
CAM_REAR_FOLDER   = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/data/1/cam_rear"

# Camera calibration
CAM_CALIB_COMMON_DIR = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/resources/cam_calib/common"
CAM_CALIB_T_PARAMS   = "/workspace/repos/K-Radar/resources/cam_calib/T_params_seq/1.pkl"

Calibration

LiDAR and Radar point clouds are reported in their own sensor frames, each offset from the vehicle's ego frame (the frame used by the GT annotations) by a fixed mounting translation. SensorCalibrationOffset (in sensor_data_utils.py) applies that translation so points line up with the GT object boxes. KRADAR_LIDAR_OFFSET and KRADAR_RADAR_OFFSET hold the K-Radar mounting offsets (x, y, z) in meters. Both LiDAR sensors (os1-128 and os2-64) share the same offset in this dataset.

N# of points by sensor

The cell below implements the CPU pipeline. It accepts either a directory of .pcd files or a single .pcd file via resolve_input_paths, and uses points_in_boxes(..., device="cpu") (a pure-NumPy implementation in sensor_data_utils.py) instead of the CUDA kernel points_in_boxes_gpu. No .cuda() / .pin_memory() calls are used anywhere in this pipeline.

Radar Voxel Occupancy Analysis

Instead of projecting the radar cube into a sparse point cloud and then testing points-in-boxes, we operate directly on the dense arr_zyx tensor. This preserves zero-power voxels and enables aggregation of raw power statistics per object. For every annotated object the following are computed:
  • radar_voxel_count – number of voxel centres inside the 3-D box.
  • radar_mean_power – mean power value (linear) of those voxels.
  • radar_max_power – peak power of those voxels.
  • radar_high_power_voxel_count – voxels whose power exceeds the 95th-percentile of the whole frame.
  • radar_occupancy_score – fraction of in-box voxels that are "high power" (high_power_voxel_count / max(voxel_count, 1)).

Camera Visibility Analysis

For each annotated object we determine whether (and how much of) it is visible in each of the four K-Radar cameras: cam_front, cam_left, cam_right, cam_rear.

Projection chain

GT boxes are in the ego frame. For each camera we have:
  • Extrinsics R (3×3 rotation) and t (3,) translation that transform a point from the ego frame to the camera frame: P_cam = R @ P_ego + t
  • Intrinsics fx, fy, px, py (focal lengths and principal point): u = fx * P_cam[0]/P_cam[2] + px v = fy * P_cam[1]/P_cam[2] + py
A point is visible if depth = P_cam[2] > 0 and 0 <= u < W, 0 <= v < H.

Visibility percentage

We sample ≥500 uniformly distributed points inside each 3-D box, project them into the camera, and report the fraction that satisfy the visibility conditions. This is a Monte-Carlo approximation of the fraction of the object volume that the camera can observe.

Unified Multi-Modal Observability

compute_multimodal_observability iterates over every annotated object and merges LiDAR, Radar, and Camera metrics into a single row per object. The output Polars DataFrame is exported as both .parquet and .csv.
